title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Number of Covers per Customer and per Booking
content:
Two counting rules govern how many covers of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims` may exist: one looks at the customer, the other at the booking.

## Clause

1. **Per customer.** No ceiling is set on the number of covers one customer may hold. A customer may hold as many covers as it has shipments, each cover belonging to a single shipment.
2. **Per booking.** A booking may carry no more than one cover in force at any moment. A cover counts as in force while its status is quoted, active, claim open or claim closed.
3. **New quotation.** A fresh cover may be quoted for a booking only where the booking's earlier cover has been cancelled or has expired.

Whether a booking already carries a cover in force is read from the line's cover records for that booking, not from what the customer says about it.

## Consequence for the statutory record

The statutory tier, `AHL Standard Carrier Liability`, is itself a cover on the booking. Transferring a shipment out of statutory liability into a CargoCare product accordingly calls for the quoted statutory record to be cancelled so that the new quotation can be made, and that cancellation is available only while the statutory record still stands at the quoted status.

## Input, judgement, output

| Status of the booking's existing cover | In force? | Does this rule allow a new quotation on the booking? |
|---|---|---|
| quoted | yes | no |
| active | yes | no |
| claim open | yes | no |
| claim closed | yes | no |
| cancelled | no | not barred by this rule |
| expired | no | not barred by this rule |
| no cover on record | no | not barred by this rule |

## Points of judgement

- *A customer ships forty bookings in a month (hypothetical). Is any of them refused a cover because of the number already held?* No. The count per customer is unlimited; only the one-cover-per-booking rule applies.
- *A booking's earlier cover shows a closed claim. May another cover be quoted on it?* No. A cover with a closed claim is still in force.
